fields.reasoning: workflows-are-the-rules: recoveries that belong to a step stay in that step's workflow, and the watchdog only resumes runs, so the workflow's own steps (including merge) still decide. That makes it a backstop, not a second implementation of the three bug fixes, and it never merges outside a workflow. The intent says 'rebase', but bug 01M6WBVX and the repo's practice say merge origin/main, never rebase or force-push (force-push is denied here), so the watchdog merges. Owner-attended runs are left alone, as daemonNudgeStalled already does, because the owner may be the one the run waits on. The 20m nudge reuses today's daemonNudgeText threshold; doubling it before a retry gives the session one chance to answer. Budget 2 and one CI rerun match the intent's 'rerun failed CI once' and the bug requests' 'retry once', with one spare for a stall. warn-dont-safeguard: everything is policy with defaults in rhiza.toml, and it warns (inbox, log, health) rather than blocking.
fields.statement: (1) The watchdog is the daemon-level backstop; the three bug requests stay separate and ship on their own. Each adds a first-line recovery inside its workflow step (a step retries once on a vanished go $WORK, plan reruns failed CI once, ship-change merges main on a conflict). The watchdog acts only on what those miss: a run that has stalled, or has ended on a known transient signature. It never duplicates a step's recovery while the step is still live. Its resume counts against its own per-run retry budget, separate from any step's. (2) Stalled step (no journal entry or session report past its limit), autonomous runs only: first nudge the session (today's daemonNudge). If there is still no progress after a second limit, stop the step and run resume --retry, logging one line and charging the run's budget. Once the budget is spent, leave an inbox item naming what was tried. Owner-attended runs get only the log line and an inbox item, never a stop or retry. (3) A PR with no CI because it conflicts with main: the watchdog merges origin/main into the branch and pushes normally (never rebase or force-push), then records the push in the run's ship state. If the merge conflicts, it resumes the run so the run's own conflict handling (the 01M6WBVX fixer, once shipped) takes it; until then it leaves an inbox item. A green PR its run never merged: when the run ended failed at or before its merge step, the watchdog resumes it with --retry so the workflow's own merge step merges it, and never merges outside a workflow; a live run is left alone, and a run that ended succeeded (run resume refuses --retry on it) or whose merge needs the owner gets an inbox item instead. Every recovery caused by a bug files one deduplicated bug request with the evidence. (4) Shipped defaults, as settings in settingDefs like the other daemon settings, each key of one scope: machine keys rhiza.daemon.watchdog.* as flat full-key strings under [daemon] in the root's rhiza.toml, and project keys rhiza.project.watchdog.* of the same names (all but pollBehind) in the project's git config, as rhiza.daemon.maxRuns and rhiza.project.maxRuns are today. For a project the effective value is its project key when set, else the machine key, else the default; rhiza daemon settings shows each key's value, source and scope. A workflow step may set its own stall limit as a step field, which wins for that step and is shown with the workflow, not in the settings rows. Defaults: enabled = true; agentNudge = 20m (as today) and agentRetry = 40m for agent steps; commandLimit = 30m; waitLimit = 90m for CI and PR wait steps; retryBudget = 2 per run; ciReruns = 1 per PR head, counting a rerun the step already made; pollBehind = 3 (warn when a poll takes over 3x the poll interval); fileBugs = true; autonomousOnly = true.

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run TestWatchdogPolicy covers the defaults with no watchdog key set, a machine value under [daemon] in rhiza.toml, a rhiza.project.watchdog.* key in git config giving that project's effective value over the machine key, a workflow step's stall field winning for that step, and an invalid value rejected with its key named; go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScripts/watchdog-policy shows the machine and project keys with their sources and scopes in rhiza daemon settings
fields.statement: The daemon reads its watchdog policy from settings declared in settingDefs like the other daemon settings, each key of one scope: machine keys rhiza.daemon.watchdog.* as flat full-key strings under [daemon] in the root's rhiza.toml, and project keys rhiza.project.watchdog.* of the same names (all but pollBehind) in the project's git config. For a project the effective value is its project key when set, else the machine key, else the default. A workflow step may set its own stall limit as a step field, which wins for that step. Shipped defaults: enabled = true; agentNudge = 20m and agentRetry = 40m for agent steps; commandLimit = 30m; waitLimit = 90m for CI and PR wait steps; retryBudget = 2 per run; ciReruns = 1 per PR head; pollBehind = 3 (times the poll interval); fileBugs = true; autonomousOnly = true. rhiza daemon settings lists every machine and project key with its value, source and scope

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run TestWatchdogCIRerun, with a fake gh, shows the failed jobs rerun once, the run resumed after they pass, no second rerun on the same head, no rerun of a head whose run attempt is already above 1, and a new head allowed its own rerun
fields.statement: When a run ended failed waiting on CI with red checks, the daemon reruns the PR's failed jobs once per PR head and resumes the run with --retry when they pass. A head whose failed jobs were already rerun (gh shows a run attempt above 1, as the plan step's own rerun leaves it) counts as that one rerun, so the watchdog does not rerun it again; a second red on the same head is left for the owner

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run TestWatchdogGreenUnmerged, with a fake gh, shows a resume --retry for an autonomous ship that ended failed at its merge step, nothing for a live run at its merge step, and an inbox item with no resume and no merge call both for a run that ended succeeded with its PR unmerged and when the ship stage needs the owner
fields.statement: When a run's PR is green but the run never merged it, the daemon acts by the run's state: a run still live (at its wait or merge step) is left alone; a run that ended failed at or before its merge step is resumed with --retry so the workflow's own merge step merges it, never merging outside a workflow; a run that ended succeeded with its PR unmerged (run resume refuses --retry on it), or whose workflow's merge needs the owner, gets an inbox item instead

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run TestWatchdogBugs shows one bug request queued with the run ID, step and log lines, a second matching recovery queuing none while the first request is open, a CI flake queuing none, and fileBugs = false queuing none
fields.statement: For each recovery caused by a bug (a stall, a transient failure other than a CI flake, a PR its run left unmerged or without CI) the daemon queues one bug request with the evidence (run and request IDs, step, log lines), and does not queue another while an open request already names the same recovery kind and step; fileBugs = false (rhiza.daemon.watchdog.fileBugs, or rhiza.project.watchdog.fileBugs for one project) turns this off
